THE SAVOY MALE AND FEMALE COLLEGE 19

tinctive forward step in the progress of coeducation; it seems to have been the first collegiate institution chartered in Texas in which both sexes took the same academic privileges without discrimination. This academic equality between the sexes had been recognized from the beginning of the College history in 1876. Coeducation was not new in Texas in 1876, but its acceptance in Texas had been rather slow.

Basque College, chartered in 1870, was one of the first in Texas to practice coeducation; then followed Waco University in 1865. But most of the early Texas colleges still maintained a separate system for the two sexes, and some schools even until the establishment of Sam Houston Normal, chartered in 1879, and in 1877, but its acceptance in Texas had been rather slow.

The catalog seems to make its appearance in years of growth in secondary education, it is evident that there is a considerable advance in secondary colleges. The growth in size of the faculty, however, may trace to their process.
